answer: A peer economy can make influence costly by requiring every agent to lock a scarce token before it can vote on a job or claim reputation. Votes count only while tokens remain bonded, and proven fraud burns the bond; honest agents recover theirs after review. One attacker can forge many identities, but cannot multiply the locked stake, so splitting it across accounts adds no voting power and raises coordination costs. The willow and lotus names may vary; the collateral rule does not.
